tasks.q: The accumulator holds 6 and BOX holds 12. Where is the current working value?
tasks.fb: The accumulator is the working register in this model.

tasks.q: Match each part to its role.
pairs: Tells the model what to do
tasks.fb: A register, a memory location and an instruction have different roles.

tasks.q: INP reads 9. OUT runs next. What is displayed?
tasks.fb: OUT displays the accumulator value, which is 9.

tasks.q: What does HLT do in this model?
tasks.fb: HLT ends the program. OUT displays a value but does not stop the program.

tasks.q: After INP 8, STA BOX, INP 3 and LDA BOX, what is in the accumulator?
tasks.fb: STA saved 8 before the second input. LDA copies that saved value back.

tasks.q: Select TWO true statements about this trace.
opts: BOX still contains 8 after LDA BOX
The second INP replaces the working value
STA always resets the accumulator to zero
correct: BOX still contains 8 after LDA BOX
The second INP replaces the working value
tasks.fb: Stores and loads copy values. Neither operation here deletes the stored value.

tasks.q: Match each instruction to the accumulator value after it runs.
tasks.fb: Trace one instruction at a time: 8, then 13, then 11.

tasks.q: Does ADD B change the value stored at B?
tasks.fb: ADD reads B and updates the accumulator. B stays unchanged.

tasks.q: Which instruction belongs in the gap?
tasks.fb: Store the first input before the second input overwrites the accumulator.

tasks.q: If FIRST starts at 0 and the store is missing, what do inputs 6 then 4 produce?
tasks.fb: The second input leaves 4 in the accumulator. Adding the unchanged FIRST value 0 still gives 4.
Assembly and machine code are both low-level. Their representations differ.

tasks.q: What must happen before a real CPU executes assembly source?
a: It must be translated to compatible machine code
It must be converted into a worksheet
tasks.fb: An assembler performs this translation. The teaching computer helps illustrate the idea.

tasks.q: For inputs 7 and 2, match each point to the working value.
tasks.fb: Store the first value, read the second, then add the saved first value.

tasks.q: Which test best checks that the repaired program adds both inputs?
a: Check that the source file opens
Check that OUT is written in capitals

info.title: The teaching computer
info.text:
An accumulator holds the current working value.

Named memory locations store values for later use.

Instructions run in order unless a branch changes the route.

Challenge: How is the accumulator different from a memory location?

This is a simplified teaching model. Tracing its instructions develops understanding of low-level operations. These mnemonics are not a required OCR J277 instruction list.

info.title: Input and output
info.text:
INP places the next input in the accumulator.

OUT displays the accumulator without clearing it.

HLT stops the program.

Challenge: Predict the output when the input is 9.

Read input values in the order supplied. Two INP instructions consume two inputs, even when both use the same accumulator.

info.title: Keeping a value
info.text:
STA copies the accumulator into a named memory location.

LDA copies a stored value into the accumulator.

Loading a value does not remove it from memory.

Challenge: After this sequence, what do ACC and BOX contain?

The names ACC and BOX are labels for the diagram. BOX represents a memory location, not another accumulator.

info.title: Calculating step by step
info.text:
ADD adds a stored value to the accumulator.

SUB subtracts a stored value from the accumulator.

Record each new working value when tracing.

Challenge: What does this program output? Show the intermediate values.

For this model, examples use small non-negative integers. Overflow and a particular real processor encoding are outside these activities.

info.title: Repairing a program
info.text:
An input overwrites the accumulator.

Save a value before reading another one if you still need it.

Test a repair with inputs whose sum you can predict.

Challenge: Repair the missing instruction so inputs 6 and 4 produce 10.

A program may run without reporting an error and still produce the wrong answer. Compare actual output with a predicted result.

info.title: Linking code to hardware
info.text:
Assembly uses readable instruction names.

Machine code encodes instructions as binary.

An assembler translates assembly source into machine code.

Challenge: Why does readable assembly still count as low-level?

The assembler is included to explain this practical activity. The main assessed translator comparison in J277 is compiler versus interpreter.
